The Dawning Archaic: Trap ceiling on a mediocre floor. The 53.8% GIH and low OH (47.4%) say it's dead in your hand until the graveyard fills — a P1P1 alsa of 1.9 is pack-position hype, not power. A no-immediate-impact 10-drop in a fast Converge format; only worth it in a dedicated Prismari/spell-heavy shell, and even then it's a splashy build-around, not a slam.
Rancorous Archaic: Filler. The 53.6% GIH is soup-inflated — 4-5c Converge pilots cast it for a 4/4+ trample/reach, but in a 2-color deck it's a vanilla 4/4 for five, exactly the 'begrudgingly playable' last-card LR describes. Take a real card over it.
Sundering Archaic: Bomb in soup, splashable disruption elsewhere: the 58.8% GIH is Converge-inflated by 4-5c pilots exiling MV5-6 permanents; in a 2-color deck it only removes MV≤2 on ETB, so lean on the repeatable {2} grave/deck disruption LoL and LR praise. Still first-pickable colorless, just size expectations to your color count.
Together as One: The set's premier bomb and P1P1 slam. Colorless so it slots into any deck, and even at X=4 it's a one-card game-ender (draw 4, kill their 4/4, gain 4). Converge scales with soup, but you don't need five colors — LR/LSV call it the goat. First-pick everything.
Transcendent Archaic: Solid Converge finisher, but the 57% GIH is a 4-5c soup number — X-draw scales with colors, so a 2-color deck draws 2 and discards 2, a wash. LoL's #5 payoff read holds for greedy piles; in a normal WU/UB pair it's just a 6/6 vig you play late, not a slam.
Ajani's Response: Solid removal that's unconditional destroy for {4}{W}, or a bargain {1}{W} on anything tapped (post-attack, tapped-out). LoL calls it filler and LR says it always plays fine; the 57.6% GIH splits the difference — a clean, reliable playable, just not a high pick since the cheap mode is situational.
Antiquities on the Loose: Premium white rare and a near-slam: two 2/2s now plus a flashback that returns four power with counters. 64.2% GIH / 1.9 ALSA / +9 IWD is elite and transfers cleanly to any white deck — this is a genuine two-for-one army-in-a-can, take it over most commons and role-players.
Ascendant Dustspeaker: Solid playable, quietly better than it reads. A 5-mana 3/4 flyer that pumps another creature and repeatedly exiles graveyards is the format's 'filler-plus' floor-raiser — LoL's 'Rooftop Percher.' 55% GIH; the negative iwd just means it's a curve-topper you always want anyway, and it wrecks flashback/GY decks.
Daydream: Trap, and both LR and the 48.8% GIH agree — negative IWD (-3.9) and a 1.0 grade confirm it. Blinking your own creature for one counter is a fringe combo enabler that whiffs with Reparte counters and does nothing in Lorehold. Leave it in the sideboard.
Dig Site Inventory: Role-player combat trick with rebuy. The 55.4% GIH rides its -0.8 iwd and 68% play rate — it's a cheap early inclusion, not a card you want to draw, and the flashback squeezes marginal extra value in counters/graveyard shells. Solid filler, easily cut.
Eager Glyphmage: Filler, not the powerhouse it looked like — LoL and Numot both flag it as near-last-pick overrated, and the -1.1 IWD confirms the 3/3-plus-flyer stat line underdelivers. Play it in Silverquill if you need bodies, but don't prioritize.
Elite Interceptor: The #1 white common and a premier pick — a 1-drop 1/2 that prepares a tap/untap-plus-draw, giving a body, tempo disruption, and a card. 59.2% GIH on a common with ALSA 4.2 is elite; it over-performs everywhere, especially UR/Prismari. Never pass it early.
Emeritus of Truce: Premium first-pick removal disguised as a body: a 1WW 3/3 that makes an Inkling, and once prepared casts Swords to Plowshares. ALSA 1.8 and 58.5% GIH confirm it — LR's B/B+ conditional worry (opponent must out-creature you) barely dents it since the token narrows the gap. Take it P1P1 in any white deck.
Ennis, Debate Moderator: Trap. A 1/1 that blinks your own creature to re-trigger an ETB and slowly grows is doing almost nothing on rate — the -5.0 IWD and 50% GIH confirm it actively hurts you unless built around. Filler at best, and the DS 2.0 is right.
Erode: Premium one-mana removal that kills anything, creature or planeswalker. The basic-land ramp they get is a real cost in this grindy format, which is why IWD is only +1.6 and OH lags, but unconditional {W} instant-speed removal is exactly what soup and aggro both want. Snap it.
Graduation Day: Trap/sideboard. A W enchantment that only does anything in a dedicated Repartee spell-slinger — LR flatly calls it 'bad,' and the -2.9 iwd plus sub-51% GIH confirm it dilutes any normal deck. Skip unless you're deep in a counters-plus-targeting build.
Group Project: Solid go-wide role-player for RW Lorehold — a 2/2 token now, then a second body via flashback (tapping three creatures). 56.7% GIH with strong OH (57.7%) means it pulls weight early, not just as a synergy card. Fine playable that scales with a token board; not a high pick.
Harsh Annotation: Sideboard-y unconditional removal. Two mana kill-anything is tempting, but handing the opponent a 1/1 flyer drags it to a flat 50% GIH and a 25.6% play rate — the Inkling matters in an evasion format. Prefer conditional removal that doesn't gift a blocker/attacker.
Honorbound Page: Role-player. A 3/1 first strike that sandbags a flying-pump prepared spell is fine curve filler, but the -2.5 IWD and 41% play rate say it's the last cards in your deck, not a card you reach for.
Informed Inkwright: Premium 1W 2/2 that spits a 1/1 flier every time you target a creature with a spell — a snowball in any spells-matter shell (Silverquill/Prismari). 61.5% GIH, ALSA 1.8, IWD +6.2: it takes over games and stacks hard. High pick.
Inkshape Demonstrator: Sticky WB/spells role-player — a 3W 3/4 with ward 2 that grows and gains lifelink off targeted instants/sorceries. Flat +0.1 IWD says it's a curve-filler not a bomb, but the ward makes it resilient. Best in Silverquill (WB) per LR; a fine body anywhere.
Interjection: A one-mana +2/+2-and-first-strike trick that blows out combat and pushes damage. The 55.6% GIH looks fine but the -0.3 IWD and 29% play rate mark it as a narrow tempo/aggro tool you don't want multiples of — role-player for creature-dense white beatdown.
Joined Researchers: Solid two-drop role-player: a 2/2 first striker that occasionally symmetrically draws six. 54.9% GIH with negative IWD says it's a fine early body, not a payoff — the prepared Divergent-style draw is a wash you rarely want to fire. Playable filler, not a priority.
Owlin Historian: Solid common flyer. A 2/3 flyer for 2W that surveils on entry and grows whenever cards leave your graveyard fits any W deck and feeds GY synergies as upside. 55% GIH with 62% play rate — a reliable early evasive body you're happy to run.
Practiced Offense: Premium — a game-ending pump-your-whole-team plus double strike or lifelink for 5 mana over two casts, and the numbers are elite (64.7% GIH, +9.8 IWD, 92% play). Marshall's groan-test pick; even on one evasive creature it just wins. First-pick white, an anthem finisher any counters or go-wide deck wants.
Primary Research: Solid value playable. Five-mana reanimate-a-3-drop plus a repeating draw-on-graveyard-churn engine — 54.9% GIH at 68% play is a fine midrange include, best in graveyard/self-mill shells where the end-step trigger fires reliably.
Quill-Blade Laureate: Solid early pick and a top-3 white uncommon per LoL: 89% play rate and 3.6 ALSA reflect that the repeatable double-strike pump is a premier Repartee enabler and combat finisher. Happily take multiples in a spells-matter white deck.
Rapier Wit: Filler cantrip. Tap-plus-stun (only on your turn) plus draw is real tempo, but a 30.6% play rate and negative IWD say it rarely makes decks — the tap is too fleeting outside a dedicated tempo plan. Sideboard/last-few-slots.
Rehearsed Debater: Filler 3/3 vig that needs targeted spells to matter. Negative IWD (-1.8) and 54.7% GIH with a late 6.5 ALSA mark it as a late-pick body — playable in a spells-heavy WU/WR deck, cuttable otherwise.
Restoration Seminar: Provisional read: the 57.4% GIH and 2.1 ALSA are mythic-selection artifacts (it's picked early regardless), not a signal it's good. {5}{W}{W} to reanimate one permanent with a huge paradigm setup cost is exactly the 'not convinced' LR D-grade — needs a stacked graveyard to justify seven mana. Late-game payoff, low priority.
Shattered Acolyte: Fine 1W 2/2 lifelink that maindecks its own sideboard tech — sac to blow up an artifact or enchantment matters when Potioner's Trove and Roles are everywhere. 55.9% GIH is a clean two-drop number; a reliable, unexciting playable.
Soaring Stoneglider: Solid aggressive uncommon. Effectively a 3-mana 4/3 flying vigilance when you can exile two GY cards (or a 5-drop otherwise) — the flexible cost keeps it live early or late. 53.7% GIH and a huge 74% play rate; a clean beater for any W tempo/flyers deck.
Spiritcall Enthusiast: Role-player, and the 51.9% GIH plus negative IWD says it underdelivers — the prepared trigger needs a token to fire, and a vanilla 3/3 body until then is why play rate sits at 44%. A Lorehold tokens payoff (also triggers off Treasures) but replaceable; take the payoffs over this.
Stand Up for Yourself: Solid, reliable removal — 57% GIH at 86.5% play, LR's 'reliable' C+. Kills nearly everything relevant in a beatdown format where power 3+ is the norm; only whiffs on small utility creatures. High-priority white pick.
Stirring Hopesinger: Bomb — 62.7% GIH, +7.7 IWD, 1.6 ALSA and near-universal play back LR's 'absolutely absurd.' A 2W lifelink flier that team-pumps on every creature-targeting instant/sorcery snowballs any Silverquill/Prismari spells deck. First-pick.
Stone Docent: Solid, low-demand role-player — a 1W 3/1 that trades or races early and recycles from the graveyard for life plus surveil late. "Asks nothing of you": 56.5% GIH with an aggressive body. Fine filler for any white deck, unexciting.
Summoned Dromedary: Recursive 4/3 vig that buys itself back for 1W from the yard — decent grind value. But 54.2% GIH and negative IWD say the recursion rarely swings games; a serviceable common-slot beater, not a priority.
Banishing Betrayal: Solid tempo interaction — {1}{U} bounce any nonland permanent plus surveil 1 to smooth draws. LR bumped it C-/C+ as 'buying time is always great,' and the +4.4 IWD backs that; the gap between 50.7% OH and 57.9% GD confirms it's a reactive card you want to draw into, not open with. Good role-player.
Brush Off: Premium counter for Prismari/soup: {1}{U} to stop an instant or sorcery, {2}{U}{U} for anything else. The GD 60.7 vs OH 53.3 split is textbook reactive-card — much better drawn than in your opener. LoL flags it as the big mover for soup mirrors; take it highly in spell-dense decks.
Campus Composer: Fine role-player, not the bomb it looked. A 3/4 ward 2 that later spawns a 3/3 flyer is real value, but LoL's retro flags it OVER-RATED — the 'can't believe it isn't great' blue card. 54% GIH; the +2.7 iwd is prepared-payoff synergy, not raw power. Playable, don't over-draft.
Chase Inspiration: Combat trick / sideboard card. +0/+3 and hexproof is a fog-a-block and removal-dodge that's purely reactive — the 54.3% GIH rides on a 22% play rate of dedicated pilots, and OH (51%) is weak because it's dead without a target. Filler protection; play it only if short on tricks.
Deluge Virtuoso: Role-player prowess payoff, trap outside UR spells. The stun-tap ETB is real tempo, but the Opus buffs only pay off with density; 51.9% GIH and LoL/LR both warn it locks you blue. Playable in a committed spells deck, a trap as a speculative early pick.
Divergent Equation: Synergy role-player, discount the 58% GIH: the {X}-cost line is inflated by big-mana soup pilots, and the split (51.6% OH vs 61.3% drawn) marks it as a late-game recursion card, not an early play. Good in a spells deck with mana to burn, filler otherwise.
Echocasting Symposium: Strong blue value engine — a 4UU paradigm that copies your best creature every turn once online. GD 60.5% vs OH 53.5% and IWD +8.8 mark it as a snowball that's great drawn, mediocre stranded in the opener. Solid in slower UR/Quandrix soup, not a bomb.
Emeritus of Ideation: Bomb, first-pick-any-deck. A 3UU 5/5 flyer with ward 2 that ETBs with Ancestral Recall stapled on and can re-trigger. 64.5% GIH, +14.5 IWD, ALSA 1.4 — the numbers are as loud as LR's A+. This just wins games.
Encouraging Aviator: Role-player. A 2/3 flyer that keeps re-casting 'grant flying' via prepared is fine but low-impact — the 50.4% GIH is unexciting. LoL likes it as a repeatable Opus/spells trigger in Prismari (UR); outside that it's a body. Playable where the flying-grant enables evasion or Opus payoffs.
Essence Scatter: Solid Prismari/soup counter, but decode the hype: the prerelease "high creature count" read was moderated once games proved low-creature. Still a fine 57% playable — sequence around it and don't pass into open blue. Better as a role card than a first pick.
Exhibition Tidecaller: Premium Prismari (UR) engine, borderline bomb. A 1-mana 0/2 that mills 3 (or 10 on a 5+ mana spell) per instant/sorcery snowballs games — 60.3% GIH, +9.6 iwd, ALSA 2.4. LR's key note: DON'T deploy it before turn 6 so opponents can't cheaply kill it. A slam in any spell deck.
Flow State: Strong blue card-selection at a great rate — 56.8% GIH, +5.5 IWD, 85% play back it. Dig three for one, and once you've got an instant and sorcery in yard it's two-for-one card advantage. A smooth Prismari/spellslinger enabler that also just fixes draws; solid early pick.
Fractal Anomaly: Trap/near-unplayable. It's a 0/0 unless you've drawn extra cards this turn — 48.5% GIH, 8.9% play, DS 1.0 all confirm it does nothing without a draw-two engine online first. Skip unless you're deep in a dedicated card-draw Quandrix build.
Fractalize: Filler combat trick at best — 18% play rate, 2.3 grade and a 51.4% GIH. Turning a creature into an X+1 vanilla body is win-more or a mediocre pseudo-pump; leave it in the board most drafts.
Harmonized Trio: Trap. A free Brainstorm stapled to a 1/1 that dies to everything and needs two other creatures tapped to fire — LR marks it DOWN. 53.3% GIH and 60% play rate flatter a card that does little; skip unless you're deep on cheap spell-value. Filler.
Homesickness: Solid tempo-plus-card-advantage instant: draw 2 and stun-tap two attackers/blockers. 55.8% GIH with a big gap between OH (51.3) and GD (58.4) — it's a mid-game answer you want to draw into, not open. Good glue in any blue deck, especially defensive UB/UW.
Hydro-Channeler: A defensive 1/3 that ramps you into instants and sorceries with fixing — quietly good in any spells-matters deck (Prismari/Quandrix). The +3.1 IWD and 74% play rate show it pulls its weight as an enabler; the 1/3 body also blocks early. Solid role-player, not a slam.
Jadzi, Steward of Fate: Strong flexible blue rare: a 2/4 that loots twice on entry, with a late-game X/X Fractal-swarm mode when flooded. 59.5% GIH, 1.9 ALSA, +8.3 IWD — the body-plus-selection floor plays in any blue deck and the back half scales in Quandrix/soup. High pick.
Landscape Painter: Solid value common. A 2-mana 2/1 that later draws two off its prepared side is a clean two-for-one for U tempo/card-advantage decks. 53.6% GIH with a positive +2.6 iwd; unspectacular body but the built-in refuel keeps it always maindeckable.
Mana Sculpt: The best counterspell in the set — hard Counter for 1UU that refunds you the mana on your next turn if you control a Wizard (easy in this Wizard-dense format). 57.9% GIH and +7.8 IWD confirm it plays great even off-synergy. Premium blue interaction.
Mathemagics: Bomb. Doubling draws (typically 4-8 cards for X=2-3) with a +12.7 iwd and 2.4 ALSA — this refills and buries opponents. The {X}{X} means it scales best in ramp/multicolor, but even a straight 2-color blue deck games it as a premium payoff. First-pick card advantage.
Matterbending Mage: Solid Quandrix tempo playable: 58.2% GIH and +5.6 IWD on a 2U 2/2 that bounces a blocker on ETB and turns your X-spells into unblockable finishers. The evasion rider is real upside in a spells-and-{X} shell.
Muse Seeker: Below-average filler. A 1U 1/2 looter that only draws-net-positive off 5-mana spells; otherwise it's a fragile rummage on a body that dies in a removal-dense format. LR marks it DOWN. 52.6% GIH confirms the weak read.
Muse's Encouragement: Underplayed (34.8% PR) but the 3/3 flyer token plus surveil 2 is real value at 4U. The 52.6% GIH is dragged down by low play; the +3.3 IWD says it overperforms when included. A fine flex playable for UR/UW spells decks.
Orysa, Tide Choreographer: A 2/2 that draws two, dropping to {1}{U} once your board has 10 toughness — LR's 'bad but I love it anyway.' The +3.3 IWD reflects the two-card refuel, but at full price a 4U do-nothing body is mediocre. Playable value card in a defensive toughness-matters build, filler elsewhere.
Pensive Professor: Card-advantage engine that pulls its weight in spell decks: increment grows the 0/2 and each counter draws. 58.6% GIH / +8.4 IWD / 2.1 ALSA is a real payoff, but the 0/2 body dies to Tome Blast, so it wants Prismari/soup with cheap spells to trigger it, not an empty board.
Procrastinate: Fringe-playable pseudo-removal. XU taps and stacks 2X stun counters, locking a threat down for several turns — LR upgrades it to 'one of your best late-game removal spells' when flooded. 52% GIH but only 36% play; it never kills anything, so treat it as a tempo/lock filler, not real removal.
Quick Study: Solid card-advantage common — instant-speed Divination is always maindeckable, and 56.1% GIH with +5.1 IWD says it earns its slot in any blue deck. The 60% play rate and modest OH just reflect that it's a mid-game refuel, not a tempo play. Reliable role-player.
Run Behind: Solid tempo. Effectively three-mana against an attacker to tuck it top or bottom of library — 57.1% GIH, +4.9 iwd, great against Fractal tokens per LoL. Not permanent answer but reliable; LoL prefers cheaper Banishing Betrayal, so it's a secondary interaction pick.
Skycoach Conductor: Solid rare — flash flying vigilance 2/3 that reuses your best ETB every turn (LR's 'free Eldrazi Displacer'). 57% GIH plus the prepared blink mode make it flexible value; strong in any ETB-heavy blue deck.
Spellbook Seeker: Filler. A 3U 3/3 flier is fine, but the prepared loot-two-discard-two is card-neutral and the whole package underwhelms — 26.8% play rate and 50.6% GIH say most decks cut it. Late-pick only.
Tester of the Tangential: Cheap Increment engine that snowballs off big spells and redistributes counters. 53.9% GIH, +3.2 IWD — a role-player that rewards a high-curve spells deck. Fragile 1/1 base; good in dedicated UR/UG builds, mediocre in beatdown.
Textbook Tabulator: Defensive spells payoff — a 0/3 wall that surveils 2 on entry and grows via Increment as you cast bigger spells. The 31% play rate and 7.1 ALSA say it's a niche late-table pick; +3.4 IWD only in a deck that leverages the block-and-dig. Role-player for controlling Quandrix/Prismari, filler otherwise.
Wisdom of Ages: Prismari/soup control payoff, not a midrange card — the OH 49.8 vs GD 61.7 chasm proves it's dead in your opener and backbreaking once you have a spell-filled yard. LoL calls it the best over-the-top control finisher (insane with Visionary's Dance). Only draft it if you're the grindy deck.
Adventurous Eater: Solid common. A 2B 3/2 that later grows a creature and gains a life off the prepared side — a fine curve-filler two-for-one, strongest in Witherbloom (BG) counters/lifegain. 54% GIH, 67% play; the negative iwd just reflects it being a proactive early body, not a catch-up card.
Arcane Omens: Underrated, and the numbers back LoL over the 4B grade — 59.8% GIH and +9.0 IWD are real. But heed the doctrine: this is THE Converge payoff, so its WR is inflated by 4-5c pilots who discard 5. In a 2-color deck it's a 5-mana discard-3, still good but not the snap-concede card; discount accordingly.
Arnyn, Deathbloom Botanist: Role-player. A 2/2 deathtouch that trades up is fine, but the drain trigger needs a sac/token stream that a 2-color BW deck rarely sustains — -2.1 iwd and 50.5% GIH say the payoff mostly idles. Playable body, unexciting.
Burrog Banemaker: Role-player. A one-mana deathtouch body that trades up and firebreathes as a late mana sink is fine early defense, but the 54.4% GIH and +0.7 IWD mark it as a curve-filler, not a priority.
Cheerful Osteomancer: Filler. A 3B 4/2 that prepares graveyard recursion looks fine but under-performed — black wasn't the creature-based late-game base it needed. 51.4% GIH and negative IWD; a replaceable body. Bottom of the deck.
Cost of Brilliance: Solid aggressive-black playable: draw 2 for 2 life plus a +1/+1 counter, feeding Repartee/aggro. LoL nails it — great in Silverquill/Witherbloom (WB/BG) midrange, BAD in soup/control where better draw exists. LR's B- and 57.4% GIH agree; prioritize in the right deck.
Decorum Dissertation: Repeatable card advantage — {3}{B}{B} draws two, and paradigm lets you free-cast a copy every turn thereafter. The 56.2% GIH and 2.0 ALSA (mythic) confirm a strong engine, though LoL warns the 2-life-per-cast can backfire into lifegain decks and you needn't keep firing it. Premium late-game engine; take highly.
Dissection Practice: Flexible {B} instant: a drain plus a +1/+1 and a -1/-1 to split across combat. 58% GIH at one mana makes it a sneaky-good trick/finisher-enabler that ambushes small creatures and pushes damage. Solid maindeck playable in any black deck.
Emeritus of Woe: Bomb. A 3B mythic 5/4 that comes with Demonic Tutor stapled on — LR: 'the demonic tutor is JUST upside' on top of an already-great body, and it re-arms whenever two creatures die. ALSA 1.5, 59% GIH, 89% play. First-pick, snap it every time.
End of the Hunt: Premium removal — 1B edict-that-you-choose isn't quite targeted, but exiling the opponent's biggest creature/planeswalker for two mana is efficient and answers bombs. 58.3% GIH, 87% play, alsa 3.3 mark it as a top-table black common. Cheap, splashable, always in the deck.
Eternal Student: TRAP — LoL confirmed this every episode as the card whose badness defines the format. The 54.2% GIH flatters a homeless value engine; a 4/2 that makes two 1/1 flyers from the yard is too small-ball for a midrange-dead format. Take format-relevant cards over it.
Foolish Fate: Premium removal — unconditional Murder at 2.7 ALSA and 92% play rate, with the infusion lifeloss a free finisher in any lifegain shell. Take it highly in black; kills anything.
Forum Necroscribe: Disappointing five-drop. A 5B 5/4 with ward-discard whose repartee reanimator needs you to be a creature-targeting spells deck to matter, which black rarely is. LR grades it D in practice at 51% — playable body, not a payoff.
Grave Researcher: Trap-ish rare — reads like reanimation but plays like a Centaur Courser. ALSA 2.1 and 88% PR reflect the hype, but 55.5% GIH and only +1.5 IWD expose it: LoL is right that Witherbloom/Silverquill want creatures to trade, not fill the yard. A fine 3/3, not a bomb.
Last Gasp: Premium cheap removal — {1}{B} for -3/-3 kills most of the curve at instant speed. LR's 'no deck doesn't want it' and the 57.4% GIH at 88.7% play rate make this a top-tier common; LoL flags it as elite for Converge/Witherbloom. First-pick-quality interaction.
Lecturing Scornmage: Aggressive one-drop for spell-slinging black — OH 60.9 vs GD 55.8 shows it wants to hit the board early and snowball as you target creatures. Fine in Silverquill/Prismari repartee shells, weak topdecked. Take as a curve-filler, not a bomb.
Leech Collector: Filler that wants Witherbloom (BG). A 1B 2/2 that drains 2 the first time you gain life each turn — fine in a dedicated lifegain shell, mediocre elsewhere. 51.8% GIH and -2.4 iwd say it's a role-player, not a slam; play it in the deck that turns it on, cut it otherwise.
Masterful Flourish: Combat trick — +1/+0 and indestructible for one mana is a cheap blowout that beats removal and wins combat, but it's reactive filler (35% play, +0.6 IWD). The 56.1% GIH is respectable for a trick; run one or two if your deck wants combat interaction, otherwise sideboard.
Melancholic Poet: Solid two-drop for spells decks. A 2/2 that drains 1 each time you target a creature with an instant/sorcery — 56% GIH at 79% play, and its OH ~= GD means it's good early and late. Real payoff in Prismari/Lorehold spells shells.
Moseo, Vein's New Dean: Near-bomb Witherbloom rare: 60.1% GIH, 4.0 grade, and a 2B flyer that makes a lifegain Pest then recurs creatures every end step you've gained life. Self-enabling engine that grinds soup out — high pick.
Poisoner's Apprentice: Solid Witherbloom role-player — a 2B 2/2 that snaps off -4/-4 removal when you've gained life, trivial in a BG lifegain shell. 55.3% GIH, 73.7% play. Conditional but the condition is easy in its home; a real reason to be in the lifegain plan.
Postmortem Professor: Sneaky-strong aggressive 2-drop: recurs itself from the yard by exiling instants/sorceries, drains on attack. Big 63.5% OH_WR and 60.1% GIH, DS 4.0 — a Silverquill/WB spells engine that's hard to beat down. High pick in aggressive black.
Pox Plague: Unplayable. {B}{B}{B}{B}{B} for a symmetrical loss-of-everything wrecks your own board as much as theirs — LR's F and the 0.4% play rate (null WR) are unanimous. Never maindeck; there is no build that wants it.
Pull from the Grave: Grindy value at replacement level: 30.5% play rate and flat IWD say it's a sideboard-y late-game card, not a maindeck staple. LR nails it — first copy is fine recursion, second is a dead card. Only soup/BG grind decks want it, and only one.
Rabid Attack: Sideboard/trap. Mass +1/+0 with death-draw reads like a blowout but LR flags it DOWN — 'looks good, doesn't deliver.' 50.4% GIH and a telling 22% play rate; needs a wide board and rarely two-for-ones cleanly. Leave it in the board for combat-heavy matchups.
Ral Zarek, Guest Lecturer: Grindy planeswalker that underperforms its rarity — 54.6% GIH and a 2.6 grade for a 3-loyalty mythic that mostly surveils or discards a card. The -2 reanimation and coin-flip ult are slow value in a fast format. A fine Witherbloom/Silverquill midrange engine, but a role-player, not a bomb; don't over-draft the mythic tag.
Scathing Shadelock: Role-player. A 4/6 for five that also gives a creature +2/+0 deathtouch via prepared is a durable, flexible body, but 52.4% GIH and -1.2 iwd mark it as slow ballast, not a driver. Fine defensive playable in a grindy BW/BG deck.
Scheming Silvertongue: Strong rare — a 1B 1/3 flying lifelink that becomes a repeatable Sign in Blood once you gain 2+ life (trivial in Witherbloom). 59% GIH and 1.9 ALSA; evasive card-advantage engine, take early.
Send in the Pest: Modest playable, better in aggressive Witherbloom than the numbers-inflating grind. LoL calls it a terrible Virus Beetle because games went huge; LR likes it as WB/BG fuel. 55.0% GIH is fine — a discard-plus-lifegain-token that's a role-player, not a pick.
Sneering Shadewriter: Filler flyer — a 4B 3/3 evasive with a 2-point drain ETB. Below-water 52.7% GIH and negative IWD, 41% PR; the flying and lifeswing are relevant late, but this is a last-few-cards inclusion, not a maindeck lock.
Tragedy Feaster: A 2BB 7/6 trampling ward creature that's a huge threat when you can feed the Infusion sac each turn — pests, lands, tokens. The 55.1% GIH and 2.8 ALSA reflect real power, but LR's 'easy to screw up' is real: without steady lifegain or fodder it eats your board. Strong aggressive top-end in Witherbloom (BG).
Ulna Alley Shopkeep: Filler bordering on unplayable: a 2/3 menace that needs incidental lifegain to become a 4/3. 49% GIH, 13.5% play, 1.0 grade — the infusion condition is too unreliable and the base body too small for a format that punishes vanilla three-drops. Leave it in the pool.
Wander Off: Reliable common removal. 3B instant, exile any creature — unconditional, and LoL notes exile matters against the format's recursion/flashback. 55.8% GIH, 87% play. Not flashy at four mana but this is the removal that makes B a splashable base; take it highly.
Withering Curse: Real but conditional sweeper — -2/-2 to all is a genuine board-swing, and it upgrades to a full wrath if you gained life (trivial in BG/WB lifegain shells). 53.5% GIH is modest because it clips your own board too, but as one of the format's few wraths it's high value in the right deck. Solid, not premium.
Ancestral Anger: Filler cantrip trick. Replaces itself while granting trample and +1/+0 (scaling only if you run multiples), but a single copy is negligible — 52.8% GIH, 16.4% play. Marginal in a spells/prowess deck for the free draw; not a maindeck priority.
Archaic's Agony: Converge trap for 2-color decks — the 56.1% GIH is propped up by 4-5c pilots; at two colors it's 2 damage for five mana, hence the 48% play rate and 6.2 ALSA. Only maindeck it in a genuine 3+ color soup where the impulse-draw kicks in.
Artistic Process: Premium flexible red — the format's answer to fatties (6 damage), a mini-sweeper (2 to each of theirs), or a 3/3 haste flier, all off one card. 56.8% GIH and 85.8% play in a double-red cost; the RR is real but it's a high pick in any red/Prismari deck.
Blazing Firesinger: Trap. A 2R 2/3 that prepares into a Dark Ritual for RRRRR you almost never usefully spend. Sub-50% GIH, DS 1.5, 38% PR — the ritual half is a build-around with no payoff here. Sideboard.
Charging Strifeknight: Solid 3-drop that experts talked themselves down on — a 3/3 haste that taps to loot is fine but 'under-delivers' per LoL and Numot. The 56.8% GIH and 81% play rate say it's a perfectly good playable, just not the bomb the prerelease hype suggested. Take it as a reliable red body, not a priority.
Choreographed Sparks: Trap. A {R}{R} spell-copier that does nothing without a strong target already on the stack — 44.3% GIH, 40.4% OH and 9.8% play confirm LR's "not interested." Unplayable outside a dedicated combo that doesn't exist here.
Duel Tactics: Role-player removal. R deals 1 with a can't-block rider and flashback for repeat value, but 1 damage kills little in this midrange format — hence 36% play despite a fine 54.7% GIH (conditioned on decks that could use it as a finisher/tempo tool). A cheap situational pick, not a maindeck lock.
Emeritus of Conflict: Premium — a 1R 2/2 first strike that hands you a free Lightning Bolt once you've cast three spells, and in a spell-dense format that's routine. LR's A- and the 86.5% play rate, alsa 2.2, agree. Removal stapled to a body; a top red pick for any spellslinger deck.
Expressive Firedancer: Role-player prowess payoff. Grows out of burn range and gains double strike off 5-mana spells — LoL likes it, but LR's C- notes the UR aggro deck never materialized. 55.3% GIH is fine in a real spells shell; a filler beater without one.
Flashback: Synergy playable, not a standalone card — the OH/drawn gap (48.5% vs 57.4%) shows it needs a stocked graveyard of impactful spells to matter. Fine in a dedicated Prismari/Lorehold spells deck; near-unplayable without targets.
Garrison Excavator: Solid Lorehold body. A 3R 3/4 menace that pumps out 2/2 spirits whenever cards leave your graveyard — easy to trigger in RW's leaves-the-graveyard shell. 56.7% GIH; a resilient, evasive threat that grinds. Good early red pick.
Goblin Glasswright: Playable common — a 1R 2/2 that prepares a Treasure, smoothing mana and fueling Converge/spells. 53.9% GIH and +1.6 IWD make it a fine early body with fixing upside; solid in UR/RW spells or any Converge splash.
Heated Argument: Playable removal that kills nearly anything — {4}{R} for 6 damage, with 2 to the face if you exile from your yard. 'Playable, not exciting' per LR; the 5.4 ALSA and clunky five-mana cost keep it mid-priority. Good filler interaction when you need more kill spells, but the OH/GD gap (51.8/57.5) marks it a card you'd rather draw than open.
Impractical Joke: Premium cheap red removal — {R} sorcery for 3 that also shuts off prevention/lifegain, which is relevant in this life-gain-soaked format. 58.5% GIH, 2.9 ALSA, 93% play; part of red's deep removal suite. Take it high alongside Tome Blast and Abrade.
Improvisation Capstone: Bomb. A 5RR Paradigm free-cast engine that fires every turn once resolved, snowballing tempo and cards — 62.5% GIH, +11.3 iwd, ALSA 1.8. LR's B+ undersells the live data; a top-tier build-around finisher in any R deck. First-pick material.
Living History: Solid RW value engine — a 2/2 token on ETB plus a repeatable +2/+0 on attack once anything left your yard, which Lorehold does naturally. 56.3% GIH with strong OH (56.8%) shows it pulls weight early. Good Lorehold playable; the graveyard condition is easy to satisfy.
Maelstrom Artisan: Underwhelming rare. A 3/2 haste that also gets a free nonbasic Stone Rain via prepared — but land destruction is marginal in a 2-color format and the body is small; 51.2% GIH, DS 1.9, 36.6% play all agree. Fringe playable, low pick priority.
Magmablood Archaic: Solid spells payoff that survives the Converge discount: hybrid {2/R} mana makes it castable and it still enters as a 4/4 trample/reach on two colors, with the per-spell anthem a real overrun in a Prismari deck. 86% play rate; good, just not the 5-color monster.
Mica, Reader of Ruins: Niche build-around. A 3R 4/4 ward that copies your spells by saccing artifacts — needs a dedicated artifact-plus-spells engine most decks don't have. 29.0% play rate and 53.0% GIH; the body alone is fine but the payoff rarely fires. Low pick outside a focused shell.
Molten-Core Maestro: Excellent spells-deck engine and near-lock in UR/RW. A 1R 2/2 menace that grows on every instant/sorcery and ramps red off big ones. 59.7% GIH, +6.9 IWD, 93% PR, ALSA 1.9 — snowballs games. High pick in any spells build.
Pigment Wrangler: Mediocre. A 4/4 flyer is a fine body, but the prepared spell-copy is a narrow payoff and the 51% GIH with -0.4 IWD shows it barely moves the needle even at 68% play. Role-player in a spell-copy Prismari build; the DS 2.3 is fair — take bodies over it.
Rearing Embermare: Filler five-drop: a 4/5 reach/haste vanilla. 49.7% GIH and 9.4% play say the format has better things to do at five, and a 5-toughness body that does nothing on ETB is exactly the kind of vanilla the guide warns against. Deep bench only.
Rubble Rouser: Premium common — the best red common if your deck can use it. A 2R 1/4 that loots on ETB, brick-walls aggro, and turns GY cards into ramp-plus-reach damage; solves the dead-removal problem and feeds Prismari GY plans. 57.8% GIH; take it early in any R deck.
Seize the Spoils: Role-player card advantage — discard one, draw two plus a Treasure smooths mana and fuels graveyard synergies. 54.9% GIH is fine but the discard cost and 52% play rate keep it from premium. Best in spell/Treasure decks that want the fixing; solid filler otherwise.
Steal the Show: Flexible spells payoff. Loot-your-hand and/or burn scaling with instants/sorceries in yard — 54.5% GIH but a strong +3.0 iwd and LR's B mark it as a real card that overperforms once you're drawn in. Best in dedicated Prismari; modes-both mid/late.
Strife Scholar: Filler — 50.9% GIH, 24.6% play rate, 2.1 grade. A 3/2 that eventually sandbags two 2/2 tokens is slow and unimpressive; a late-deck body only when short on playables.
Tablet of Discovery: Solid enabler for UR spells — a 2R rock that ramps two mana for instants/sorceries and cracks off a mill-and-play on entry. 56.7% GIH, IWD +4.2. LR: a touch stronger than Trove once you're committed blue-red, but take fixing first early. Good in Prismari.
Tackle Artist: Fine trample body for a spells deck — 4/3 that grows off your instants/sorceries. But 52.7% GIH and only 47% PR say it's a role-player, not a driver: it needs a critical mass of cheap spells to outpace removal. Playable filler in UR/RW.
Thunderdrum Soloist: A 1/3 reach body that pings opponents on every instant/sorcery, scaling to 3 damage on 5+-mana spells — a genuine Prismari (UR) spells payoff that also blocks flyers. The +3.0 IWD and 76% play rate confirm it's a solid engine in the right deck; role-player-to-good depending on your spell count.
Tome Blast: Top red common — Firebolt with flashback, elite cheap removal (57.3% GIH, 89.9% play). LoL uses it as the litmus test for aggro creature-sizing: if your two-drops get two-for-one'd by it, you're built wrong. Snap-pick removal that goes in every red deck.
Unsubtle Mockery: Premium red removal. 2R instant, 4 damage plus a surveil — LR notes it's the red common LSV took most when offered. 57.5% GIH and a 93% play rate; clean, cheap, kills nearly everything at instant speed. Prioritize it over most non-rare red cards.
Zealous Lorecaster: Playable value common — a 4/4 for six that regrows your best instant or sorcery is fair-rate in Prismari. 54.6% GIH with a big gap between OH (49.2%) and GD (57.5%) confirms it's a mid-game topdeck, not a tempo play. Solid role-player; the infinite-ish loops LoL notes are cute upside, not the reason to play it.
Aberrant Manawurm: Role-player defensive body. A 2/5 trample that swings huge off any spell cast — good blocker that punches back in a spells deck, but 50.9% GIH and +1.2 iwd say it's a supporting piece, not a bomb. Playable in Quandrix/Prismari, skippable elsewhere.
Additive Evolution: Solid Quandrix engine — 57.3% GIH and +5.2 IWD on a 3GG enchantment that lands a 3/3 Fractal immediately then grows a creature and grants vigilance each combat. Sticky, uninteractive value; good midrange payoff.
Ambitious Augmenter: Premium green — a G 1/1 that grows every big spell and, when it dies, dumps its counters onto a fresh Fractal, so removal doesn't fully answer it. 60.4% GIH, OH 63.3%, IWD +8.5: one of the scariest turn-1 plays. High pick in any green deck.
Burrog Barrage: Solid green fight-removal at 1G — your creature deals its power to theirs, with a spells-matters pump. 55.2% GIH and +2.5 IWD; the gap (OH 52.2 vs GD 57.2) says it's a good draw. Reliable removal for any green deck, better in spells-heavy GU/GR.
Chelonian Tackle: Weak fight spell — {2}{G} gives +0/+10 then fights, so your creature survives most exchanges, but sorcery-speed and needing a good creature make it clunky. The 50.2% GIH, -1.5 IWD and 33% play rate all say filler; DS 1.5 is right. Last-resort removal for green decks short on interaction.
Comforting Counsel: Trap build-around: needs five lifegain triggers before it does anything, then wants a board to buff. 45.2% GIH, -6.5 IWD, 1.0 grade — LR's "really bad green enchantment nobody plays." Even dedicated Witherbloom lifegain doesn't want it. Never maindeck.
Efflorescence: Sideboard/near-cut. A 2G trick giving two counters, with trample+indestructible only if you gained life that turn — a fragile do-nothing that gets blown out. 49.4% GIH and a damning 6.7% play rate. Even in Witherbloom lifegain it's the last card in the deck.
Emeritus of Abundance: Premium — a 2G 3/4 vigilance that enters prepared, so you get an immediate Regrowth plus a recurring one at eight lands. LR's A- and the elite line (59.3% GIH, +7.8 IWD, alsa 1.6, 86% play) confirm it. A green first-pick: value engine on a hard-to-block body.
Emil, Vastlands Roamer: Solid GU/counters engine. A 3/3 for three that grants trample to your counter creatures and pumps out scaling Fractals late — 53% GIH at 72% play. The activated ability is mana-hungry, so it's a good-not-great body first, payoff second in Quandrix.
Environmental Scientist: Premium early pick — 61.1% GIH and a huge +9.0 IWD on a 1G 2/2 that fetches a basic. LoL calls it easy-mode fixing into Converge/splashes and LR 'somehow free.' Slam it, especially when your mana is shaky.
Follow the Lumarets: Filler card selection. Dig-four for a creature/land (two if you gained life) is slow and card-parity — 25.1% play rate and 51.7% GIH say most decks pass it. Marginal even in Witherbloom. Last picks.
Germination Practicum: Premium green go-wide payoff — two counters on your whole team, then Paradigm re-casts it free every turn. 58.4% GIH, +7.9 IWD, ALSA 1.6 — a board-dominating engine in creature-heavy GW/BG. High pick that runs away with parity boards.
Glorious Decay: Sideboard card. A flexible {1}{G} instant that hits artifacts, flyers, or graveyards while cantripping — but the 6.4% play rate says it's almost never maindecked. The 51.3% GIH is a small-sample artifact of targeted boarding. Keep it in the board for flyers/artifact matchups.
Hungry Graffalon: Filler: a 3/4 reach that increments slowly, but 14.8% play and 50.7% GIH say the payoff is too grindy to matter. A fine blocker in a pinch, nothing you draft on purpose. Bench material.
Infirmary Healer: Fine role-player. A 1G 2/3 that later gains X life off the prepared side — a solid early body with a lifegain trigger for Witherbloom (BG) payoffs. 53.6% GIH, 71% play; unexciting but flexible, and the lifegain rider carries real synergy value in the right shell.
Lumaret's Favor: Combat trick / filler — +2/+4 with an infusion copy if you gained life, but the 52.8% GIH and 18% play rate say it rarely earns a slot even in lifegain BG. A conditional trick with a fiddly payoff; sideboard unless your deck is deep in lifegain triggers.
Mindful Biomancer: Fine role-player two-drop. Gains 1 life on ETB and firebreathes +2/+2 as a mana sink — 53.4% GIH, respectable early filler that scales into the late game. Unexciting but a reasonable green two-drop to fill the curve.
Noxious Newt: Good role-player — a 1/2 deathtouch mana dork does double duty as ramp/fixing and a blocker that trades up. 55.4% GIH, 84% play rate; efficient glue for green Converge decks.
Oracle's Restoration: Cut. A G pump-plus-draw-plus-life is a wash of a card that does nothing to the board — 1.0 grade, 13.7% play, sub-50% GIH. Effectively unplayable outside a spell-count corner case. Sideboard.
Pestbrood Sloth: Great green common-slot beater — 4/4 reach at 3G that leaves two lifegain Pests when it dies, so it always trades up. 58.8% GIH, +5.9 IWD, 86% PR — sticky value that fits every green deck, especially BG Witherbloom's aristocrats.
Planar Engineering: Ramp-and-fix that nets two lands and fixes any colors — the +6.3 IWD is real and helps stumble into a curve. But sacrificing two lands for four tapped basics is heavy tempo loss and mostly a Converge/soup enabler; a tight 2-color deck rarely needs it, so discount the number. Playable in greedy multicolor builds only.
Shopkeeper's Bane: Marginal aggressive body — 4/2 trample that drips 2 life on attack. 53.1% GIH at ~47% play is the definition of last-cuttable: dies to any burn and the lifegain is incidental. Playable if you're short on bodies in Witherbloom, otherwise skip.
Slumbering Trudge: Strong beatdown finisher, but deck-specific. XG for a 6/6 that comes down faster the more you pay — LoL: a midrange/beatdown card that's awkward in Prismari and weak in soup, so DON'T splash for it. 59.1% GIH with 61.6% OH-WR (it's a curve-out card). Excellent in dedicated GX, discount elsewhere.
Snarl Song: Premium build-around, but discount per doctrine — the 61.7% GIH and +11.2 IWD are Converge-inflated by 4-5c pilots who make two huge tokens. LoL flags it splashable on one green pip and the #2 Converge payoff. In a 2-color deck it's two ~1/1s and 1 life — mediocre; only a slam if you're committed to Converge fixing.
Studious First-Year: Premium green common — LR's 'best green common,' 'did it all.' A 1/1 that prepares a Rampant Growth: fixes colors, ramps, then leaves a body. 56.9% GIH with a huge +5.3 iwd and 3.8 ALSA. Enables greedy splashes; high pick priority in any green deck.
Tenured Concocter: Playable big body, not a priority — 4/5 vigilance that draws when targeted and swings as a 6/5 with lifegain. LoL likes it bullying soup, but the 34% play rate and 2.2 grade say it's a Witherbloom curve-topper, not a slam.
Thornfist Striker: Solid Witherbloom body — a 2G 3/3 with ward-1 that turns your team into a +1/+0 trampling attack when you've gained life. 56.0% GIH; a resilient overrun threat that fits the better (aggressive) BG plan. Good role-player, not a bomb.
Topiary Lecturer: Ramp/dork with upside — grows via Increment and taps for G equal to its power. +4.2 IWD is strong for a 1/2, but 54.5% GIH marks it a role-player: it accelerates your big spells but dies to everything. Good in ramp-y GU/GR, skippable in aggro.
Vastlands Scavenger: Strong — a 1GG 4/4 deathtouch that trades up immediately, with a prepared self-mill that dumps a fresh creature onto the battlefield for {4}{G}. The 57.1% GIH, 2.3 ALSA and +4.9 IWD confirm a premium green rare that gives a body now and value later. Take highly.
Wild Hypothesis: Flexible-but-fringe green card: a scalable Fractal plus surveil 2 for card selection. 52.2% GIH / 30.9% play with OH 48.2 vs GD 54.7 marks it as a mediocre late-game topdeck. Fine in Quandrix ramp as a mana sink, replacement-level elsewhere.
Wildgrowth Archaic: Converge trap for 2-color decks — discount the 56.4% GIH hard. The counter engine only pops with 3+ colors of mana, so that inflated WR is riding 4-5c pilots. LoL is blunt: best as a T2 GG play that grows creatures, but a 'mediocre 4-mana 2/2 elsewhere.' In a straight 2-color deck it's filler.
Zimone's Experiment: Role-player dig — look five, grab up to two creatures/lands, effectively a ramp-plus-card-selection sorcery. 52.3% GIH and 34% play mark it as fringe: it's card disadvantage if you whiff on hits. Playable in a creature/land-dense green deck, but a filler-tier pick.
Abigale, Poet Laureate: Solid WB uncommon. A 2/3 flyer for three that repeatedly grows your team via prepared counters whenever you cast creatures — 54.6% GIH at 77% play. Evasive body plus a slow snowball engine; a fine, reliable Silverquill role-player, not a bomb.
Abstract Paintmage: Build-around filler — 50.2% GIH, 2.1 grade, 48% play. A 2/2 that rituals two mana only usable on instants/sorceries needs a dedicated spells deck to justify a fragile body; skip in normal Prismari.
Applied Geometry: Strong Quandrix payoff — copy any permanent as a 6/6 Fractal (a haste-less flier if you copy an evasive creature, or a mana doubler off a rock). 57.9% GIH, IWD +7.8, ALSA 2.4. It's a clean two-color GU card, so the multicolor read holds; a real high pick.
Ark of Hunger: Bomb artifact, first-pick — every card leaving your yard drains 1 and gains 1, plus a card-advantage mill engine. 63.1% GIH, +9.4 IWD, ALSA 2.0, and LSV literally 'never beats it.' Colorless-castable value machine that grinds anyone out. Take it high.
Aziza, Mage Tower Captain: Build-around Lorehold (RW) payoff — a 2/2 that copies each instant/sorcery if you tap three creatures. Note the multicolor GIH (53.2%) is inflated by soup pilots; the -1.1 IWD and OH>GD gap say she under-delivers when you can't reliably chain spells. LR's B+ assumes a spells-and-bodies deck; discount her for a generic 2-color list.
Berta, Wise Extrapolator: Good Quandrix/GU-soup engine: a 1/4 that ramps any-color mana as it grows and makes Fractals as a mana sink. 55.3% GIH, 2.3 ALSA, +5.4 IWD — the fixing-plus-payoff bundle enables the greedy ramp-soup base. Strong pick for GU, less so for a lean two-color deck.
Blech, Loafing Pest: Strong Witherbloom (BG) payoff. A 1BG 3/4 that dumps counters on your whole Pest/Bat/Insect/Snake/Spider board every time you gain life — a fast snowball in the lifegain deck. 59.1% GIH, +7.1 iwd, ALSA 2.5. A top-tier build-around gold card; premium if you're in BG lifegain.
Bogwater Lumaret: Solid BG Witherbloom enabler — a 2/2 for two whose repeatable lifegain-on-ETB turns on your infusion and lifegain payoffs (Pest Mascot, Withering Curse). 55.1% GIH with good OH (55.7%) shows it curves fine on its own. Good glue common for lifegain, replaceable filler elsewhere.
Borrowed Knowledge: Unplayable — 46.1% GIH, 3.1% play, DS 1.0. Discarding your hand to draw off the opponent's hand size is a symmetrical gamble that usually loses you material and tempo. Sideboard curio at best; leave it in the pack.
Cauldron of Essence: Role-player rare — Numot warns the recursion often arrives too late and dies to exile, LR grades it B for creature-heavy Witherbloom. The 51.4% OH vs 57.4% drawn split confirms it's a slow value engine, not a bomb; play it only in a sacrifice shell.
Colorstorm Stallion: Premium Prismari threat and near-bomb — a 1UR 3/3 haste ward that grows on every spell and clones itself off any 5-mana spell. 62.5% GIH, IWD +12.1 on a two-color card is a genuine number, not soup inflation. Snowballs fast in UR spells. High pick.
Colossus of the Blood Age: Strong Lorehold (RW) top-end — 6/6 that ETBs for 6 life-swing (3 damage + 3 life) and refills your hand when it dies. 58.5% GIH, +3.4 IWD; the OH/GD gap says it's better drawn than opening. A closer that trades or draws either way; high pick in RW.
Conciliator's Duelist: Strong but color-demanding — {W}{W}{B}{B} for a 4/3 that draws, drains, and repeatedly blinks creatures whenever you target with a spell. The 59.7% GIH here is a genuinely good Silverquill (WB) build number, only lightly soup-inflated given the tight double-double cost. LR's 'mana hurdle is real but worth it' — high pick if you're committed WB.
Cuboid Colony: Good Quandrix two-drop: flash flying trample with increment, so it ambushes and grows. LR loves it, Numot shrugs ("usually a final-build cut") — split it toward LR since 56.2% GIH / +5 IWD is a genuine tempo body. Solid GU playable, not a bomb.
Dina's Guidance: Trap. A 1BG instant that only fetches a creature to hand or GY — no board impact, pure card-neutral tutoring that's far too slow for Limited. 45.4% GIH and a brutal 7.6% play rate confirm it: don't play it. Build-around bin only.
Elemental Mascot: Trap — LR downgraded it and the numbers are unremarkable (54.6% GIH inflated by dedicated pilots at 55% play). A 1/4 flyer that grows only when you chain spells, but the UR aggro deck that wants it doesn't really exist. A defensive role-player at best; don't prioritize the gold card.
Embrace the Paradox: Good GU card advantage. Draw three at instant speed with a free land drop — 56.3% GIH and +5.2 iwd make it a strong refuel/finisher in Quandrix. Five mana is steep for pure card draw, but the tempo of the extra land smooths it. Solid playable.
Essenceknit Scholar: Solid Witherbloom uncommon — hybrid-castable 3/1 that adds a lifegain Pest and draws whenever a creature dies. 58% GIH, 80% play; self-enabling card advantage in any sac/lifegain deck.
Fix What's Broken: Trap. It reanimates only permanents of exactly MV X (they forgot "or less"), so it's a narrow, low-curve build-around, not a value reanimator. 46.4% GIH, IWD -5.1, 18.2% play — the data confirms it's broken in the bad way. Sideboard.
Fractal Mascot: Overcosted 6/6 trample with a stun-tap ETB — fine tempo but 6 mana in GU. Low 43.8% PR and weak 49.5% OH_WR flag it as clunky; the +3.6 IWD and Numot's Echo-target note say it shines mainly as a copy/blink target. A slow finisher, not a priority.
Fractal Tender: Filler, per Numot's 'fine but I don't care for it.' A 3/3 ward that spawns a 3/3 Fractal when Increment triggers is a fair Quandrix (GU) value engine, but the 53.3% GIH is soup-inflated by 4-5c pilots — discount for a 2-color deck. Playable role-player, not a build-around.
Geometer's Arthropod: Synergy build-around: a 1/4 wall that digs when you cast X-spells. 54.8% GIH but only 39.8% play means the number comes from the Quandrix/soup decks stuffed with X-costs — outside that shell it's just a blocker. Draft it only with the X-spell density to pay it off.
Grapple with Death: Solid BG removal. 1BG sorcery destroying an artifact or creature with a life gain rider — LR's B+ flexible removal that also pings Witherbloom lifegain triggers. 56.4% GIH, 84% play. Sorcery-speed is the only knock; a reliable early pick for any BG deck.
Growth Curve: Trap — a 1.0 grade and a dismal 47.8% GIH (11.8% play) confirm it. Doubling counters does nothing off an empty creature and is a two-card combo that dies to removal for a blowout. Even in UG counters this is too win-more; leave it in the box.
Hardened Academic: Premium Lorehold two-drop, near-bomb. 2/1 flying haste for two that is enabler (discard for lifelink) and payoff (counters when cards leave yard) in one — LR's B+, 'you don't get more for 2 mana.' 60.6% GIH, DS 4.3, 2.6 ALSA. Slam it.
Imperious Inkmage: Role-player — a 1WB 3/3 vigilance with surveil 2 is a fine body, but the -0.2 IWD, 6.6 ALSA and 61% play rate (LSV C+) mark it as replaceable filler, not a Silverquill priority.
Inkling Mascot: Filler in Silverquill. A WB 2/2 that gains flying-plus-surveil when you target a creature with a spell is a classic C — the flying is fleeting and the body unremarkable. 56.1% GIH but negative IWD; "won't cut it from Silverquill very often." Replaceable.
Killian's Confidence: Top Silverquill (WB) common — WB pump-plus-cantrip that recurs from the yard on combat damage, so it's card-neutral engine fuel. 56.5% GIH, LR's B; the -0.1 IWD is deceptive since it's a cheap enabler, not a game-swinger. Prioritize in aggressive WB.
Kirol, History Buff: A 2/3 that becomes prepared whenever cards leave your yard, then mills and grants +2/+2 trample — a solid Lorehold (RW) graveyard-payoff commander. The 55.7% GIH and 78% play rate are decent, but the flat/negative IWD (OH>GD) shows it wants an enabled board, not to be drawn late. Good role-player where you have graveyard triggers.
Lluwen, Exchange Student: Solid Witherbloom uncommon: a 3/4 that spits out lifegain Pests and re-arms off graveyard fuel. 55.9% GIH with +3.2 IWD is a clean value body that feeds BG's better overrun plan. Good role-player, take it for the guild but not over premium removal.
Lorehold Charm: Role-player. RW instant with three narrow modes — the +1/+1 team pump is the only reliably useful one, and LR calls it 'one of the weaker charms' Marshall tended not to play. 53.5% GIH but only 47% play. A fine 20th-25th card in Lorehold, not a high pick.
Lorehold, the Historian: Bomb — a 5/5 flying haste for five that immediately threatens the game and grants miracle plus card filtering. 57.9% GIH, alsa 1.6, 89% play mark it a first-pick. The stat is honest (it wins on its own body); the miracle/loot engine is gravy in a spell deck.
Mind into Matter: Excellent GU finisher. Draw X then cheat a permanent of MV X into play — a one-card refuel-plus-threat, 57.9% GIH with +7.6 iwd. Some inflation from ramp/multicolor pilots on the {X} cost, but it's a genuine payoff in any real Quandrix deck. High pick.
Mind Roots: Situational filler — Numot notes opponents can dump a small hand to blank it, so it only shines against a depleted hand; the ramp-a-land upside is minor. 53.1% GIH, 2.5 grade; a marginal Witherbloom inclusion.
Molten Note: Premium RW removal and reach — X damage to a creature scaled by mana spent, plus an untap for a crew/second-combat blowout, with flashback for a second use. 59.4% GIH, 84.8% play. The X is a removal knob, not soup inflation; a high pick in Lorehold.
Moment of Reckoning: Bomb — choose-up-to-4 modal Vindicate/reanimate that 'turns any board into a win.' 63.3% GIH, +9.9 IWD, DS 4.5. The 3WWBB cost is real but this is exactly the WB payoff worth building toward; take it P1 and commit to Silverburn.
Nita, Forum Conciliator: Weak build-around. The anthem on 'cast a spell you don't own' plus the sac-to-steal ability needs a spell-copy/theft shell to function; the 51.4% GIH, -2.3 IWD and 46% play rate say it flounders in a normal deck. Silverquill (WB) niche pick only; DS 2.1 is fair.
Old-Growth Educator: Solid BG body: a 4/4 vigilance/reach that becomes a 6/6 with any incidental lifegain. 53.9% GIH is a fine but unspectacular four-drop — reliable stats, no evasion or card advantage. A dependable Witherbloom midrange creature, mid-pick material.
Paradox Surveyor: Solid Quandrix (UG) uncommon. A 3/3 reach that digs five deep for a land or {X}-cost card — real card advantage plus a defensive body that fits the ramp/spells plan. 58.5% GIH, +6.5 iwd, 77% play. A dependable midrange pickup; take it solidly.
Pest Mascot: Solid BG lifegain payoff — a 2/3 trample for three that snowballs off every lifegain trigger, which Witherbloom generates constantly. 53.2% GIH is modest because it needs the engine, but in the right shell it grows into a real threat. Good role-player; unexciting outside lifegain.
Practiced Scrollsmith: Premium Lorehold engine — LR's B+ 'hallmark card, if this isn't good the deck doesn't work.' A 3/2 first strike for three that rebuys a spell from your yard. 59% GIH at 85% play. Strong body plus repeatable value; top-tier RW uncommon.
Prismari Charm: Flexible Prismari playable — modal dig/ping/bounce gives real value across game states (LR B, 'slightly worse than Silverquill's'). 56.7% GIH; a fine, unexciting two-drop that always does something.
Prismari, the Inspiration: Overrated mythic — a 5UR 7/7 flier with storm that needs a spell-dense board to pop off, and by then a vanilla flier often just wins. OH 48.5% vs GD 57.1% flags it as a clunky topdeck-reliant card; 2.8 grade, 54.2% GIH. A fine finisher, not a slam.
Proctor's Gaze: Strong GU (Quandrix) instant — bounce any nonland plus ramp a basic, tempo and fixing in one. 57.8% GIH, +6.1 IWD; the OH/GD gap (54.5 vs 59.8) says it's a great draw. Flexible answer/enabler; high pick in Quandrix, splashable elsewhere.
Professor Dellian Fel: Bomb. A three-loyalty planeswalker at {2}{B}{G} that stabilizes life, draws, and removes a creature with -3 — the 62.7% GIH, 87% play, 1.4 ALSA and +11.7 IWD are elite even after discounting soup inflation (a walker this cheap warps games in any Witherbloom/BG deck). First-pick the format.
Pterafractyl: Scaling flier that's fine in soup: X/X evasion plus 2 life for {X}{G}{U}. The OH 49.0 vs GD 56.3 gap shows it's weak early and good drawn/late as a mana sink. LR pegs it "fine in soup" — a Quandrix/ramp playable, not a card you prioritize.
Pursue the Past: Premium common — the #1 common in the format by win rate. RW gain 2, loot into draw 2, with flashback for a second helping: the Lorehold card-advantage engine. LR walked it up from C to top of the list. 59.1% GIH, 70% play. Prioritize highly whenever you're RW.
Quandrix Charm: Premium UG flexibility — a soft counter, an enchantment answer, or a 5/5 pump-trick all on one instant, which LR calls power-level top. 57.6% GIH and +6.2 IWD confirm it plays great. A top Quandrix uncommon; modal cards like this always earn their slot.
Quandrix, the Proof: Bomb. A 6/6 flying trample with cascade that also gives ALL your instants/sorceries cascade — 61.2% GIH, +11.6 iwd, 1.5 ALSA. Even discounting the multicolor/cascade halo, the raw evasive body wins games alone; the spell-cascade engine is backbreaking. First pick.
Rapturous Moment: Mediocre big-mana payoff — 4UR to loot three and ritual UURRR only pays off if you can dump the mana, hence the 49.1% OH vs 55.7% drawn split and 47% play. Situational Prismari finisher-enabler, not a maindeck staple.
Render Speechless: Underrated — LoL's biggest mover-up and the best non-rare answer to soup: a hand-peek discard plus a team pump that also pushes damage. 57.4% GIH on just 54.2% play means it's under-drafted and over-delivers. Splashable into Prismari; grab it in WB.
Resonating Lute: Build-around bomb for dedicated UR spells — doubles your lands into instant/sorcery mana plus a Library-style draw engine. LR's A and 'won in a landslide' back the 56.1% GIH (deflated by non-spells decks); +6.7 IWD. Slam in Prismari, near-unplayable outside it.
Root Manipulation: Under-rated finisher — LoL calls it the best overrun in a while because menace beats trample when board counts are low, plus the lifegain buffers the alpha strike. The 52.7% GIH understates it (top-end cards drawn early inflate the loss), and the OH/GD gap (49.8/54.6) shows it wins games when you have the board. Witherbloom's (BG) premium top-end.
Sanar, Unfinished Genius: Strong Prismari engine: a 0/4 wall that tutors any instant/sorcery and drips Treasures once you've cast a spell. 58.8% GIH, +7.6 IWD, 85% play — the fixing-plus-card-quality makes it a soup/UR-control glue piece. High uncommon pick for spell decks.
Scolding Administrator: Premium Silverquill (WB) uncommon — a 'pushed card.' A WB 2/2 menace that grows out of burn range off targeted spells and passes its counters on death. Note the standout 62.9% OH-WR: it's a proactive aggressive threat you want in your opener. 60.4% GIH; a top pick for WB.
Silverquill Charm: The best charm in the set (LR) and a premium WB gold card — counters, edict-exile on power-2, or a 3-point drain, all at instant speed for two. 59.5% GIH, 78% play, alsa 4.2 back it. Flexible removal-plus-reach; a high pick in any WB deck.
Silverquill, the Disputant: Premium bomb body. A 4/4 flying vigilance for four is elite on rate alone; casualty on every instant/sorcery is upside gravy. The 55.2% GIH reads modest for a mythic, but the 1.9 ALSA and clean evasive stats confirm a slam — don't overthink the WR.
Snooping Page: Solid Silverquill card-advantage engine — a 2/3 that goes unblockable on creature-targeting spells then draws on connection (LR: your opponent feels bad). 55.8% GIH, 80% play; recurring value in a Repartee deck.
Social Snub: Weak. A 1WB edict that copies itself with a creature out reads fine but edicts are poor in a token/board format, and 10.8% play with 51.2% GIH buries it. Sideboard vs a light-creature deck at best.
Spectacular Skywhale: Downgraded — a 2UR 1/4 flyer that needs spells to attack and folds entirely to bounce ('watch it hit the bottom of their library'). Sub-water 52.2% GIH, DS 2.3. A fragile Opus payoff; playable filler in UR spells, never a priority.
Spirit Mascot: Solid Lorehold (RW) common — a 2/2 for two that grows every time cards leave your graveyard, which fires often in a recursion/exile-matters deck. The 55.5% GIH and 75% play rate are good for a common; LSV's 'I hope' C+ panned out. Reliable early body that snowballs, but flat IWD means it's a build-piece, not a bomb.
Splatter Technique: Near-bomb for Prismari/soup — a Draw Four OR a 4-damage wrath is the best kind of flexibility. 61% GIH / +11 IWD is elite, but discount the ceiling: the {U}{U}{R}{R} cost means much of that number comes from committed 4-5c soup pilots. In a real UR deck it's still a slam; in a splashy build it may sit uncastable.
Stadium Tidalmage: Fine gold body, low priority. A 2UR 4/4 that loots on ETB and each attack is decent value, but the ALSA 7.1 / 38% play rate show most Prismari decks pass it. 54.1% GIH is respectable when played; a serviceable filler beater, not a card you draft the archetype around.
Startled Relic Sloth: Premium RW body — a 4/4 trample lifelink for four is above-rate stats, and the graveyard-exile is relevant hate in a set full of flashback/recursion. 57.3% GIH and 83% play confirm it's a strong Lorehold curve-topper. Solid pick; the lifelink also feeds infusion payoffs.
Stirring Honormancer: Solid Silverquill five-drop — LR's B+ 'premium.' A 4/5 that digs deep (X = your creature count) to find your best card while stocking the yard — 57.9% GIH at 73% play. Strong body plus card selection that feeds graveyard payoffs. High-priority WB pick.
Stress Dream: Premium — 60.1% GIH, +8.6 IWD, 4.0 grade. Five damage killing nearly anything AND a dig-two is removal plus card advantage on one card; LR says don't underrate it. High Prismari pick.
Suspend Aggression: Solid Lorehold tempo removal — a 1RW instant that exiles any nonland permanent (they get it back plus your top card, so it's temporary, not clean). 57.3% GIH, 73.5% play. Good in a proactive aggro shell where the tempo swing wins before it returns. Good pick.
Tam, Observant Sequencer: Underwhelming GU legend — a 4/3 that prepares a cantrip on landfall. The 52.4% GIH and weak 48.9% OH_WR show it's slow and land-dependent; +2.3 IWD from grinders. A serviceable body with incidental value, not a build-around. Mid pick in Quandrix.
Teacher's Pest: Efficient recurring threat — a {B}{G} menace attacker that gains life and buys itself back for {B}{G} from the yard, feeding Witherbloom (BG) sacrifice and lifegain. The 54.6% GIH and 79% play rate mark a solid two-drop; the recursion makes it great sac fodder for Tragedy Feaster and friends.
Traumatic Critique: Premium UR removal-plus-card-advantage: scalable X damage to anything, then draw two and discard. 60.3% GIH, 2.0 ALSA, +9.8 IWD, castable as early as three mana — it's a cube finisher for a reason. Top Prismari/soup pick, take over most gold cards.
Vibrant Outburst: Premium Prismari (UR) removal. UR instant for 3 damage anywhere plus a tap — LR: 'kills and tempos at the same time,' and it can hit face. 58.8% GIH, +7.4 iwd, 88% play. One of UR's best uncommons; take it highly and note the reach it adds to the burn plan.
Vicious Rivalry: Premium removal / rare sweeper — one of the format's only wraths, scaling to clear everything at mana value X while the life-payment feeds lifegain synergies. LR's A and 58.9% GIH, +7.3 IWD confirm it. A top BG pick; flexible one-sided-ish board control is scarce here.
Visionary's Dance: Underrated over-performer per LoL. Two 3/3 flyers for seven is clunky, but both halves are great and its value climbs with rebuy (Wisdom of Ages) — one of the few cards whose worth rises mid-draft. 56.4% GIH, +5.6 iwd. Strong UR playable, prioritize if you're in Prismari.
Wilt in the Heat: Good removal — 5 damage with exile rider, and it's a Lorehold 'build-around Terminate' that drops to two mana once a card leaves your graveyard. 56.9% GIH; premium in a graveyard/spells shell, still fine at full cost.
Witherbloom Charm: Flexible BG role-player — a two-mana modal instant giving sac-for-two-cards, 5 life, or kill-MV2-or-less. "Fine, not exciting": the removal mode is narrow and 53.9% GIH is average. A serviceable playable in Witherbloom, not a priority.
Witherbloom, the Balancer: Trap mythic — a 6/6 flying deathtoucher that's cheap only with a wide board, but 8 mana base and the affinity payoff rarely lines up. Sub-water 50.5% GIH, +0.3 IWD, DS 1.9 despite ALSA 2.1 hype. Overdrafted; it's a mediocre finisher, not the bomb its rarity suggests.
Zaffai and the Tempests: Clunky top-end — a 5/7 that free-casts one instant/sorcery per turn is powerful but the {5}{U}{R} cost shows in the huge OH/GD split (46.4/54.2): dead early, strong once you're stabilized. The 51.5% GIH and 41% play rate say it's a Prismari (UR) win-more you can't always cast. Build-around finisher, not a slam.
Biblioplex Tomekeeper: Trap. A 4-mana 3/4 whose ETB toggles the prepare mechanic that never mattered — LR's "worst card, teased synergy and did nothing." 45.5% GIH, 2.1% play, 1.0 grade. Do not play.
Diary of Dreams: Trap — don't run it. A 2-mana book that starts activating at 5 mana and only scales with a heavy spell count; LR rates it D in practice ('don't put it in your deck') and Numot cut it late in Silverquill for lacking permanents. 51.7% GIH flatters a card that's too slow; skip.
Mage Tower Referee: Filler — a 2-mana 2/1 that grows only off multicolor spells, and the 53.8% GIH with 28% play says it's marginal. Colorless so any deck can run it, but the payoff is thin in a 2-color build. Late-pick body for a gold-heavy soup deck; otherwise skip.
Page, Loose Leaf: Filler. A 0/2 mana rock whose Grandeur payoff requires a second copy to dig for spells — 52.7% GIH but 8.0 ALSA and 15.7% play say it rarely makes decks. Marginal ramp/fixing in a spells build; not a maindeck card in most.
Potioner's Trove: Format-defining common — LoL calls it the GOAT common/glue, LR flags it as the single most important common (D on paper, #1 in practice). 3-mana any-color fixing plus 2-life-a-turn that reorders the whole draft; take over almost everything once you have a spells payoff.
Strixhaven Skycoach: Solid colorless playable — a {3} 3/2 flier that tutors a basic to hand (fixing plus a body, dodging Essence Scatter). 58.9% GIH; a two-for-one for assertive decks, but it needs bodies to crew 2, so worse at ~10-creature counts. Good in board-based decks.
Deathcap Glade: Solid BG dual land — untapped after two lands, fixes Witherbloom perfectly. 55.7% GIH and +3.1 IWD reflect fixing value in a Converge-adjacent format. Good early pick if you're in or near BG; fixing is at a premium here.
Dreamroot Cascade: Premium fixing — a GU dual that enters untapped once you have two other lands, so it's essentially a painless dual for Quandrix or any G/U splash. The 56.6% GIH and +5.2 IWD reflect the enormous value of consistent mana in a Converge format. High pick; lands like this enable your splashes.
Fields of Strife: Playable Lorehold fixing: a RW tapland with a late-game surveil mana sink. 56.9% GIH is a land-inflated number, but RW aggro/soup happily runs on-color duals — take it once you're in the guild, snapping it before the gold two-drops wheel.
Forum of Amity: Solid fixing. A WB tapland that also surveils for 2WB late — free card selection stapled to your mana. 55.9% GIH, 73% play; the tapped-land cost is minor and the surveil is real upside in a grindy Silverquill deck. Take it as good dual-land glue.
Great Hall of the Biblioplex: Premium land — colorless, any-color spell fixing that becomes a 2/4 Wizard late, making it the best Converge fixing (LoL: take over Terramorphic). 58.8% GIH and 89% play are strong, but note that WR skews toward greedy multicolor decks. Still excellent even in a 2-color spell deck as a manland with no colored-source cost.
Paradox Gardens: Good UG fixing land with late-game surveil upside — 56.2% GIH, +4.2 iwd, 80% play. The tapland cost is negligible in a format that rewards fixing, and the surveil feeds graveyard synergies. Prioritize if you're Quandrix; splash-enabler otherwise.
Petrified Hamlet: Unplayable — null WR, 1.3% play, 0.8 grade. A niche colorless-land hate piece with no home in Limited; never maindeck.
Shattered Sanctum: The WB dual land — enters untapped with two other lands, taps for W or B. 57.2% GIH reflects fixing value in a soup/Converge format that craves colors. High pick for any WB or soup base; fixing is a real payoff here.
Skycoach Waypoint: Niche prepare-enabler land that mostly taps for colorless — a real cost in a color-hungry format. Terrible 49.7% GIH, negative IWD, 13.9% PR; LR's excitement is aspirational. Only for a dedicated prepare deck; otherwise it hurts your mana.
Spectacle Summit: Excellent fixing — a UR tapland with a late-game surveil sink, ideal for Prismari and blue/red splashes. The 56.4% GIH and 84% play rate confirm dual lands overperform in a soup format; the enters-tapped cost is minor. Prioritize mana fixing highly, especially when splashing.
Stormcarved Coast: Good Prismari/soup fixing — a UR dual that's untapped from turn three on, the mana base every spell deck wants. 56.9% GIH / +5.4 IWD reflects its value in a mana-hungry archetype. Take your duals highly once you know your lane; this is a rare-quality land.
Sundown Pass: Premium fixing. An RW dual that enters untapped once you have two other lands — near-strictly-better mana for any Lorehold deck. 57.1% GIH, +3.3 iwd, 81% play. Fixing rares like this are worth an early pick when you're committed to the colors.
Terramorphic Expanse: Premium splash fixing — omnipresent soup enabler and Lorehold graveyard-exile fodder (LoL). 56.3% GIH and 95% play reflect near-universal inclusion. For pure Converge the true 5c land is better, but for any 2-3 color deck this is the go-to fixing; take it early when your mana needs help.
Titan's Grave: Good BG fixing land — tapped dual with a late surveil sink, 55.3% GIH at 79% play. Same profile as Paradox Gardens: strong fixing that enables splashes and feeds the yard. Take it in Witherbloom; useful anywhere BG-adjacent.
Akroma's Will: Bomb finisher — even the single-mode Limited version (no commander) is a game-ending team pump: flying/vig/double-strike alpha strike or lifelink/indestructible/protection blowout. 60.1% GIH, 2.1 ALSA, 89% play; take it high.
Angel's Grace: Unplayable in Limited. A split-second fog-plus-can't-lose that only buys one turn and affects no board — 0.9 grade, 4.8% play, null WR. Constructed combo tech with no home in a draft deck. Sideboard/cut.
Armageddon: Trap in Limited — symmetrical land destruction with no board advantage to exploit it. Negative IWD (-3.0), DS 1.7, and 51.5% GIH near coinflip; the 51% PR is players misvaluing a Constructed card. Sideboard/skip.
Duty Beyond Death: Niche combat trick — sac a creature to give your team indestructible and a +1/+1 counter each, a blowout against a board wipe or alpha block but dead otherwise. The 16% play rate and -2.1 IWD say it's rarely worth a slot; the 50.7% GIH is a small, self-selected sample. Sideboard/aggro-white specialty card.
Helping Hand: Role-player reanimation: {W} to return a three-or-less creature to the battlefield tapped. 53.1% GIH / 45.9% play — a value card whose ceiling depends on a good target in the yard. Fine in grindy white decks with an ETB or two to recur, skippable otherwise.
Hop to It: Solid go-wide common. 2W for three 1/1 Rabbits — clean board presence for token/counter/anthem strategies and good with any pump or aristocrats payoff. 55.5% GIH, 62% play. Not exciting alone but a dependable enabler in white aggressive decks.
Prismatic Ending: Flexible removal, but Converge-discounted — the 56.7% GIH is buoyed by 4-5c pilots who exile big permanents. In a 2-color deck it only answers MV 0-2 (mostly 2-mana stuff), which is still fine cheap removal but not the catch-all it looks like. Good white role-player; value it as a 2-color card, not the multicolor stat.
Repel Calamity: Premium removal — 58.9% GIH, 90.7% play, DS 3.8. Two-mana kill anything with power OR toughness 4+ answers nearly every real threat in a beatdown format. LoL called it 'underwhelmed,' but the live WR overrules that stale early read. High priority.
Reprieve: Premium tempo/counter — Numot calls it a soup-mirror overperformer, 'so good.' Bouncing a spell and replacing itself is a clean two-for-zero that buys time and cantrips. 58.8% GIH, 4.0 grade; high white pick.
Requisition Raid: Situational sideboard card. A W spree that destroys an artifact and/or enchantment or pumps a team — the modes are narrow and the counter mode is weak main-deck. 50.6% GIH, 22.6% play. Board it in against artifact/enchantment decks.
Return to the Ranks: Weak — convoke mass-reanimation capped at MV 2 creatures, too narrow and slow for this format. Sub-50% GIH, -3.3 IWD, only 22.6% PR. Needs a dedicated go-wide WB shell to be even mediocre; usually a sideboard card.
Winds of Abandon: Premium removal/bomb — {1}{W} to exile any creature (they only get a basic) is elite spot removal, and the {4}{W}{W} overload is a one-sided board wipe. The 61.6% GIH, 92% play, 2.1 ALSA and +7.4 IWD are among the best in the set. Slam it first pick.
Brain Freeze: UR-mirror haymaker, not a maindeck staple everywhere — the OH 48.8 vs GD 58.7 chasm shows it's a dead opener that becomes a storm-fueled mill kill in spell-dense games. LR says "live in fear of it" in the Prismari mirror. Situational tech; great in soup, unplayable in aggro.
Cyclonic Rift: Strong tempo card, effectively a premium bounce here. In Limited it's a 1U 'return their best nonland' at instant speed — the overload for 7 rarely comes online but is a game-ender when it does. 58.7% GIH, +8.3 iwd; note the gap between 61% drawn and 54% opening-hand (it's a reactive tempo tool). High pick.
Daze: Situational counter — free (bounce an Island) is a tempo blowout on the play in a heavy-Island deck, per LR, but it's a soft Force Spike that's dead late and off-curve. 58.6% GIH rides on dedicated blue pilots. A strong tempo tool in mono-blue-leaning decks; a role-player elsewhere.
Deduce: Solid card advantage — 57.2% GIH, +5.5 iwd. Two-mana draw-plus-Clue is efficient, replaces itself now and later, and fixes/feeds any spells or artifact synergies. A clean, always-playable blue role-player; grab it to smooth your curve.
Disdainful Stroke: Solid conditional counter — LoL rates it excellent vs the slow soup mirror (a Mystical Archive overperformer) but a liability vs aggro. 56.9% GIH with +5.9 IWD; strong in grindy blue decks, sideboard-flexible against beatdown.
Flusterstorm: Weak in Limited. A U soft counter for instants/sorceries only, with storm that rarely matters in a fair draft game — you can't hold up a conditional counter reliably. 48.6% GIH, null OH. Niche vs spell-heavy soup at best; mostly sideboard.
Force of Will: Overrated import — the free mode costs a card and 1 life, and hard counters are weak in creature-driven Limited. The 56.9% GIH is deflated/noisy; DS 2.5, and you rarely want the pitch mode. A serviceable 5-mana Cancel in blue control; not the eternal all-star its name implies.
Pongify: Weak. {U} to destroy any creature is cheap, but handing the opponent a 3/3 Ape frequently costs you the trade or tempo. The 47.9% GIH and 17.6% play rate (DS 1.6) show players correctly leave it in the board; only worth it to answer a bomb you can then race. Marginal maindeck.
Preordain: Strong cantrip and deck-smoother: scry 2 then draw for {U} is premium selection for any spell deck. 56.2% GIH understates its value since it enables everything else — LR simply calls it strong. Snap it into Prismari/soup where it fuels density and finds your payoffs.
Sleight of Hand: Good cheap card selection. U sorcery digging two deep — smooths draws and enables spell/Opus payoffs cheaply. 55.9% GIH, +4.9 iwd; unglamorous but the low cost and consistency make it a fine playable, especially in spell-heavy Prismari/control shells.
Spell Pierce: Efficient, narrow interaction — one mana to tax noncreature spells shines against soup's expensive removal and Converge payoffs (LoL). 55.3% GIH with +5.2 IWD and a 43% play rate marks it maindeckable but matchup-dependent. A good cheap answer; flexible between main and side.
Stock Up: Premium card advantage — LR's 'the bar everyone else fails to clear.' Dig five, keep two for three mana: 60% GIH, +8.8 iwd, 91% play. Consistent, deck-agnostic quality selection. Top blue non-bomb; take it highly in any U deck.
Ad Nauseam: Unplayable in Limited — null WR, 6.8% play, 1.7 grade. A Constructed combo piece; the life loss is suicidal here. Leave it in the board.
Bitter Triumph: Premium black removal — a 1B instant kill-anything for a small discard/3-life cost, exactly the cheap interaction soup and aggro both crave. ALSA 2.8, 90.8% play, 57.5% GIH. Unconditional, cheap, splashable. High pick in any black deck.
Culling the Weak: Unplayable — sac a creature for BBBB with no payoff attached in this format. Null WR, 4.2% PR, DS 1.5. A combo enabler with nothing to combo into; leave it in the pack.
Dismember: Premium splashable removal — {1}{B/P}{B/P} for -5/-5, castable in any deck by paying life instead of black. The 59.1% GIH, 96.8% play rate, 1.8 ALSA and +5.4 IWD make it near-universal interaction; DS 4.1 is deserved. Take it high in any deck, black or not.
Feed the Swarm: Solid unconditional black removal: kill any creature or enchantment for {1}{B}, paying life equal to its cost. 55.5% GIH, 3.5 ALSA, 85.8% play — the enchantment reach (Roles, Comforting Counsel, Potioner's Trove) is real upside in this format. A dependable maindeck answer.
Living End: Unplayable in draft. A Suspend-3 mass reanimation sorcery with no immediate board impact and a build-around requirement no Limited deck supports. Null WR on 3% play and a 1.2 grade say it all — a constructed card that's a hate-pick or bin card here.
