Locust Spray: Filler removal with a floor — -1/-1 kills small creatures and cycles for B when dead, so it's never a total blank. But 52.1% GIH and negative IWD (-1.8) show the effect is too small in this format. A low-end role-player; the cycling is the main reason to run it.
Sheoldred's Edict: Flexible role-removal. Two-mana modal edict answers hexproof/big threats and planeswalkers, but edicts are weaker in a token-heavy format where opponents chaff off the sacrifice — 53.1% GIH, -0.2 iwd reflect that. Solid maindeck rare, not a bomb answer.
Smallpox: Unplayable — symmetric sacrifice of card, creature, and land at 5.2% play and 1.4 grade rarely favors you in a creature-based Limited game. Skip.
Stargaze: Filler card advantage. An XBB dig that pays life and is slow — LR grades it D, "you don't have time for it." 29.7% play and 55.1% GIH flatter a card that most decks cut. Marginal refuel for a grindy black control pile only.
Vampiric Tutor: Trap in Limited — pay a card's tempo and 2 life to tutor to top, but your pool has no bomb worth the card disadvantage. 46.6% GIH, -3.0 IWD, DS 1.7 confirm it's below-replacement. Skip; it's a Constructed card only.
Zombify: Weak reanimation — {3}{B} to return one creature is card-neutral and needs a fat target already in the yard to be worth the slot. The 46.8% GIH, 13% play rate and -1.8 IWD say it underperforms; DS 1.0 is right. Niche pick only if you have a genuine reanimation payoff, otherwise skip.
Abrade: Premium flexible red removal: 3 to a creature or destroy an artifact, and LoL notes incidental artifact hate is gold here (Trove/Loot/Arc everywhere). 58.1% GIH, 93.3% play — a Mystical Archive over-performer. Snap-pick alongside Tome Blast and Impractical Joke.
Big Score: Solid card advantage plus fixing. 3R instant, discard one to draw two and make two Treasures — refuels and enables splashes/Converge in one card. 55.1% GIH, 77% play; the OH-WR dip (51.8%) reflects it wanting a full hand to loot into. A good midrange pickup for any R deck.
Brotherhood's End: Premium sweeper — a modal 3-damage board wipe (or artifact sweep) for three, one of the format's scarce wraths. 59.5% GIH, +7.5 IWD, 78% play confirm it's a genuine game-swinger. A top red rare; anchors a controlling deck against go-wide boards.
Bulk Up: Trap trick — 50.8% GIH, 19.4% play, DS 1.0. Doubling power is a blowout only with an already-large or evasive creature, and the flashback costs six; too often a dead card. LoL notes it's only worth it with Deluge Virtuoso. Leave it out of most decks.
Burst Lightning: Premium removal — LR's 'premium R removal' at 93% play and 2.8 ALSA. One mana for 2 to any target, scalable to 4 late; flexible efficient burn that always makes the deck. Take highly.
Crackle with Power: Red X-finisher and near-bomb — 5X damage split across X targets is a game-ending removal/reach spell. GD 64.6% vs OH 55.2% shows it needs mana, and the X cost pulls in ramp/soup pilots, but even a plain two-color red deck wants it. 61.4% GIH; high pick.
Empty the Warrens: Build-around trap — two 1/1s for 3R with Storm you can't reliably fuel in Limited. The 55.3% GIH and +6.8 IWD are inflated by the few spells decks that spike a big turn; 40% PR. Only in a dedicated low-curve UR/RW spells engine, otherwise a bad Raise the Alarm.
Jeska's Will: Unplayable here — a Commander-designed card whose upside is gated behind controlling a commander, leaving a weak {2}{R} 'exile three, play them this turn' in Limited. Null WR at 12% play and DS 1.5 confirm it's a non-card. Do not maindeck.
Monstrous Rage: Good cheap aggressive trick: +2/+0 plus a sticky Monster Role for {R}, so it two-for-one-proofs your attacker. 56.3% GIH at 56% play — a fine combat-trick/pump for Lorehold/Silverquill aggro. Take it for proactive decks, dead in creatureless soup.
Pyretic Ritual: Unplayable. A 1R ritual for RRR with no payoff in Limited — pure mana that nets you nothing on board. Null WR on 6% play and a 1.2 grade. Never maindeck it.
Return the Favor: UR soup tech, niche but powerful — Spree lets you copy their removal or redirect it for a blowout, and it's easy to pitch in red. But the 52.6% GIH and 25% play show it's reactive and dead without a target; the big OH-to-GD gap (48.5% to 55.0%) confirms it's a late-game trick. Situational role-player for spell-dense decks.
Subterranean Tremors: Bomb sweeper. Scalable X-damage board wipe that spares your flyers, blows up artifacts at 4+, and makes an 8/8 at 8 — 59.9% GIH, +8.3 iwd, 2.1 ALSA. Some soup inflation on the {X} cost, but it's a genuine game-ender in any red deck. First-pick.
Awaken the Woods: Soft ramp bomb — the 53.9% GIH lags the 3.9 grade because it needs setup, and the OH/drawn split (51% vs 55.5%) shows it wants a full board first. XGG for X 1/1 lands is a green go-wide/ramp payoff, good with anthems but win-more on its own.
Berserk: Niche finisher/trick. A G instant that doubles a creature's power with trample but kills it at end of turn — a one-shot reach blowout, not a repeatable card. Null WR, 24.4% play, 2.3 grade. Situational; sideboard or a dedicated go-wide/evasion kill.
Crop Rotation: Unplayable — sac a land to fetch a land, pure Constructed enabler with no target worth it here. Near-zero PR (5.7%), DS 0.9. Do not draft.
Giant Growth: Marginal trick — {G} for +3/+3 is efficient and can win combat or push lethal, but at 20% play and +0.9 IWD it's a low-impact filler you'd rather have as a body. The 51.6% GIH is unexciting. Playable in a dedicated aggressive/pump green deck, sideboard-adjacent otherwise.
Glimpse of Nature: Trap build-around with no data to trust — 3.7% play, null WR, 2.3 grade. It needs a creature-flood deck that doesn't exist in this spell-and-soup format to net cards. Read is provisional but clear: leave it in the box.
Knockout Maneuver: Premium green removal. 2G puts a counter on your creature then fights their creature for its (now-boosted) power — LoL rates it over the harder-to-set-up Withering Curse. 56.6% GIH, +4.8 iwd, 79% play. Green's best common-slot removal; take it early in any G deck.
Pick Your Poison: Sideboard card — a 1.0 grade, 47.5% GIH and 5.5% play scream it. Every mode is conditional (opponent needs an artifact, enchantment, or flyer), so it's frequently a dead card maindeck. Board it in against flyers or key enchantments only.
Royal Treatment: Good protection trick — one-mana hexproof plus a permanent +1/+1 ward Role, 56.2% GIH and +4.2 iwd. Blanks removal while netting a lasting buff, great to protect a bomb or win a race. Solid green playable, especially in counters/aura shells.
Shamanic Revelation: Win-more — 50.3% GIH, 46.5% OH, 34% play. Draw-per-creature only pays off when you're already ahead on board, and then you don't need it. Fringe green top-end, usually cut.
Shared Roots: Solid ramp/fixing enabler — a 1G Rampant Growth that fetches any basic tapped, exactly the fixing soup and Converge decks want to hit multiple colors. 55.2% GIH, IWD +4.2, 74.8% play. Good glue in GU/Quandrix ramp-soup, filler in a pure aggro deck.
Triumph of the Hordes: TRAP, per LoL — no blight/poison support means it just fogs you when it doesn't kill. Sub-water 48.7% GIH, DS 1.7. A finisher that whiffs on empty boards; don't take it.
Veil of Summer: Sideboard card only — a {G} anti-blue/black hate piece that does nothing in most games. The null WR at 8.2% play and DS 0.7 confirm it's a non-maindeck card in this format. Board it in versus heavy U/B interaction, never main.
Bring to Light: Discount hard: the Converge tutor's whole value scales with colors of mana spent, so its 53.3% GIH comes from 4-5c soup pilots who hit MV4+ and cast it free — in a two-color deck you cap at MV2 and it's a clunky {3}{G}{U} for a small card. 26% play rate confirms it's a soup-only toy. Not for a lean deck.
Culling Ritual: Niche sweeper — situational, not a slam. 2BG destroys all nonland MV≤2 and ramps you off the wreckage, great against go-wide/aggro but often a dead 4-of-nothing otherwise. The +5.6 iwd is real but the 20% play rate shows it's frequently a sideboard card. Board tech more than a maindeck pick.
Deflecting Palm: Sideboard / trap — null OH/GD data and a 47.3% GIH on 17% play mark it as barely-played. Damage prevention plus reflect is a cute anti-aggro blowout but purely reactive and often dead. Read is provisional on thin data; treat as a niche sideboard answer to a big attacker.
Expressive Iteration: Premium card advantage — 57.5% GIH, +6.8 iwd, 3.2 ALSA. Two-mana three-card selection that nets two cards across the turn; deck-agnostic quality and tempo. One of the best UR/Prismari uncommons-equivalent; take it highly in any blue-red deck.
Fracture: Sideboard card — null WR and 9.6% play reflect that artifact/enchantment/planeswalker destruction is too narrow to maindeck. The 3.0 grade is for its role; bring it in against specific problem permanents.
Archaeomancer: Role-player recursion — a 2/2 that returns an instant/sorcery from your graveyard on ETB, real value in a spells deck. OH 48.3% vs GD 57.7% (IWD +4.5) shows it's a build-your-engine card, weak in the opener without spells to rebuy. Solid in UR/Prismari, filler elsewhere.
Archmage Emeritus: Exactly replacement-level here — the magecraft cantrip engine sounds great but 50.0% GIH, -1.5 IWD, and DS 2.0 say the body dies before it pays off. Playable in a dedicated UR/UW spells deck as an engine, but far weaker than its Constructed reputation.
Murmuring Mystic: Strong spells payoff — spins out a 1/1 flying Bird each time you cast an instant or sorcery, quickly building an evasive army from behind its 1/4 body. The 56.5% GIH, 90.5% play rate, 2.7 ALSA and +5.2 IWD confirm a premium engine for Prismari/Quandrix spells decks. High pick where you have the spell density.
Grim Haruspex: Solid card-advantage engine for black sacrifice/BG grind: 3B 3/2 that draws on each nontoken creature death, with morph flexibility. 54.1% GIH, 2.7 ALSA, 80.7% play — the number transfers cleanly since it's just a good rate on a repeatable draw engine. Reliable mid pick that snowballs in creature-dense decks.
Dualcaster Mage: Weak role-player. A 2R flash 2/2 that copies an instant/sorcery on the stack — needs a target on the stack to be more than a vanilla body, so it's dead in most spots. Note the ugly 45.3% OH-WR vs 53.6% drawn: it whiffs from your opener. 50.5% GIH; a fringe playable only in dedicated spell decks.
Magus of the Library: Trap on the numbers — 45.4% GIH and a brutal -6.7 IWD (worse when drawn) with a 1.6 grade, despite the rare tag. The card wants a full grip and heavy lands to snowball card draw, a build-around that flat underperforms in this format. Provisional given missing OH/GD data, but the GIH says leave it; don't be seduced by the rarity.
Sylvan Library: Overrated by its mythic tag in Limited — 51.8% GIH, -0.7 iwd. Without paying life you draw one and effectively scry; the life-loss to keep extra cards is dangerous in a beatdown format, so it plays as a modest role-player, not a bomb. Prioritize actual threats over it.
Adrix and Nev, Twincasters: Build-around trap in Limited — 48.5% GIH and 1.7 grade despite the mythic hype. Token-doubling does nothing without a dense token base, and the fragile body dies before it pays off. Only in a dedicated Quandrix go-wide deck, and even then risky.
Codie, Vociferous Codex: Niche build-around — a colorless engine that only lets you cast noncreature spells but chains value off each one. 34.4% play and 2.0 grade say most decks can't warp around the restriction. 54.3% GIH from the few dedicated spell decks that ran it; low pick outside a focused shell.
Library of Alexandria: WASHED, per LoL — T1 Library can't keep up with soup's over-the-top payoffs, and the huge OH/GD gap (67.4 vs 54.9) shows it's only great when you open it in a low-curve hand. 60% GIH is real but conditional. A fine but overrated land; take it, but don't overprioritize.
